A home airfield for the independent web

A little home. A wide-open web.

Flightstead turns the things you share from your iPhone into thoughtful pages on your own website—without handing your words, photographs, or audience to a platform.

Ready for departure

Made for the things worth keeping.

Share from the apps you already use. Flightstead recognises what arrived, gives it the right shape, and publishes it without flattening everything into the same generic post.

FS · 01

One-tap dispatch

Send a thought, link, photograph, book, song, quote, or article from the iOS share sheet.

FS · 02

Proper pages

Each kind of post gets useful structure, considered typography, and a stable address.

FS · 03

Your own identity

Choose a theme, title, profile, and custom domain. The result looks like your site.

FS · 04

A useful archive

Browse by type or date, search everything, and keep ordinary URLs that stay useful.

FS · 05

Feeds built in

Quiet by design

No visitor accounts, engagement traps, advertising network, or third-party scripts.

Your home field

Keep the keys to the hangar.

Flightstead is software you operate, not another social account. Your domain, database, uploads, and backups stay under your control.

  1. 01
    Your database is a fileSQLite keeps the archive portable, understandable, and easy to back up.
  2. 02
    Your media stays localOriginals and generated variants live in storage attached to your server.
  3. 03
    Your domain is the addressReaders, feeds, and federation all meet at your public home.
  4. 04
    Your exit remains openThe server is MIT-licensed. Keep it running, fork it, or move it.

Open skies

A small site can still travel far.

People can follow your site from Mastodon and compatible Fediverse apps. New posts travel outward while the original remains on your domain, in your design, under your control.

Pre-flight checklist

A small server, not a second career.

Flightstead is one Node process backed by SQLite. Run it on inexpensive shared hosting, a Linux server, or a machine you already manage.

Choose a home field

Bring a domain and an always-on host with SSH access.

Install and configure

Clone the server, install it, and add your domain and email settings.

Prepare the logbook

One migration command creates the SQLite database.

Pair the app

Scan the short-lived QR code to connect Flightstead and sign in.
